name: 46,XX Ovotesticular Difference of Sex Development

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Ovotesticular DSD

criteria.description: Presence of 46,XX karyotype confirmed by cytogenetic analysis
Histological identification of both ovarian and testicular tissue (ovotestis) in gonadal biopsy or surgical specimen
Clinical presentation with ambiguous external genitalia at birth or early infancy
Elevated or variable serum testosterone and anti-Müllerian hormone levels inconsistent with typical female or male profiles
Ultrasound or MRI evidence of mixed gonadal structures or Müllerian derivatives

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of 46,XX karyotype plus histological confirmation of ovotestis and clinical evidence of ambiguous genitalia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for SRY gene presence may be performed to exclude 46,XX testicular DSD.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal morphology of female internal genitalia

searchTerms: abnormal urinary and genital tract connection

laboratory: Serum hormone profile showing variable testosterone, estradiol, LH, FSH levels
Anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) levels inconsistent with typical male or female patterns
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound or MRI demonstrating presence of both ovarian and testicular tissue or Müllerian structures
other: Histopathological confirmation of ovotestis in gonadal biopsy

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of testicular tissue with variable ovarian tissue
46,XX karyotype with testicular tissue only, no ovarian tissue
Presence of SRY gene in most cases

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia at birth requiring urgent multidisciplinary evaluation
Risk of gonadal tumor necessitating early gonadal assessment
Potential for psychosocial distress and gender identity challenges
references: Lee PA, Houk CP, Ahmed SF, Hughes IA. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Pediatrics. 2006;118(2):e488-e500.
Hughes IA. Disorders of sex development: a new definition and classification. Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2008;22(1):119-134.
Ono M, Harley VR. Disorders of sex development: new genes, new concepts. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2013;9(4):229-243.
